header_summary:
A mechanism has been proposed to upgrade P2P protocol security by integrating ML-KEM-768 key establishment, enhancing protection against future quantum attacks while balancing bandwidth efficiency and security margins in line with [FIPS 203](https://csrc.nist.gov/csrc/media/Events/2025/workshop-on-guidance-for-kems/documents/papers/kemeleon-paper.pdf). Discussion centers on optimal parameter sets and whether default transmission of encapsulation keys should be required, as detailed in the [bitcoindev mailing list](https://gnusha.org/pi/bitcoindev/12a1a76d-0e27-4035-9fe8-a47524729c47n@googlegroups.com/T/#u#m85f1ad08dcf59870a50431a82801279a866e9c93).

New and revised Bitcoin Improvement Proposals (BIPs) have been published, including one from Liam Gilligan addressing open questions and inviting broad community review at [GitHub](https://github.com/liamgilligan/bips/pull/1), and another draft expanding secure, standardized payload exchange between wallets and external signers—supporting descriptors, miniscript, MuSig2, and silent payments—available for input at [GitHub](https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/pull/2353) and discussed further in the [DelvingBitcoin forum](https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/qr-based-signing-flow-payloads-in-miniscript-context/2464).

A protocol-wide constant of 16 payout slots has been suggested to standardize decentralized mining pool operations, removing reliance on hardware-specific slot claims and improving fairness for miners near participation thresholds ([source](https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/decentralized-coinbase-payout-protocols-dcpp-a-framework-for-discussion/3060/8)). Meanwhile, advanced batch signature verification and formal proof techniques—leveraging tools like Lean and [RiscZero](https://www.risczero.com)—are being explored to reduce computational verification bottlenecks, potentially enabling efficient blockchain validation for resource-constrained clients ([source](https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/a-stark-proof-of-bitcoins-utxo-set-at-block-972-500-with-circuits-proven-in-lean/3070/2)).

Significant progress has been made in designing a post-quantum address format for Bitcoin, with Zaenus et al. proposing a versatile, future-proof specification that supports various key types and ensures quantum resistance even after key disclosure. The updated draft, available at the [btc-safe GitHub repository](https://github.com/Zaenus/btc-safe/blob/4e09003f69ee276f8df1eadcc913ab98a84dbf52/docs/bip/0001-pq-address-format.m), addresses previous errors, clarifies encoding rules, details performance trade-offs, and highlights open questions around key type selection, hybrid schemes, and witness data discounts, inviting further community feedback.

recent_posts.title: BIP Proposal: ML-KEM Key Establishment
recent_posts.summary: - A transport layer upgrade mechanism proposes ML-KEM-768 for enhanced quantum-resistant key establishment in P2P.  - Key exchange involves encapsulation keys and ciphertexts, supporting bandwidth efficiency and strong connection security.  - Feedback is requested on parameter choice and advertiser behavior regarding sending encapsulation keys by default.

recent_posts.title: [BIP Proposal] Transport Feature Negotiation
recent_posts.summary: - A draft Bitcoin Improvement Proposal has been released and is available for public examination.  - The current version addresses prior unresolved issues and incorporates several key decisions.  - Community members are invited to review the proposal and provide feedback via the linked GitHub page.

recent_posts.title: [BIP Draft] Signing message encoding
recent_posts.summary: - A draft Bitcoin proposal seeks to standardize exchanges between wallets and external signers across various channels.  - Comprehensive support includes descriptors, miniscript, MuSig2 multisignature protocols, and silent payments.  - Community feedback is invited via GitHub and related forums to refine the proposed specifications.

recent_posts.title: Decentralized Coinbase Payout Protocols (DCPP): A Framework for Discussion
recent_posts.summary: - A fixed limit of 16 payout slots standardizes and ensures predictable transaction templates for all implementations.  - Consistent slot allocation removes variability from hardware differences and benefits miners near participation thresholds.  - A uniform slot count streamlines value-weighted draws, promoting both technical efficiency and fairness.

recent_posts.title: A STARK proof of Bitcoin's UTXO set at block 972,500, with circuits proven in Lean
recent_posts.summary: - Lean formalizes mathematical proofs and improves cryptographic protocol security, especially in blockchain systems.  - Hardware acceleration and batch signature verification can reduce computational burdens, benefiting lightweight blockchain clients.  - Techniques like Groth16 with STARKs significantly lower verification time, enhancing scalability and accessibility.

recent_posts.title: BIP Draft Post-Quantum Address Format (bc1z) using ML-DSA-65
recent_posts.summary: - The proposal updates Bitcoin's address format for quantum resistance and future signature scheme support.  - Key changes include enhanced sighash mechanisms, new key type bytes, and compliance with existing standards.  - Performance impacts, key type selection, and open implementation questions are highlighted for community discussion.

active_posts.title: BIP Draft Post-Quantum Address Format (bc1z) using ML-DSA-65
active_posts.summary: - A new `bc1z` Bitcoin address format uses ML-DSA-65 for quantum-resistant, secure signatures.  - Backward compatibility is maintained via a soft fork, with open-source tools for adoption and monitoring.  - The community is encouraged to review address design, migration strategies, and the timing of proactive adoption.

active_posts.title: [BIP Proposal] Stale Tip Relay
active_posts.summary: - The `staletip` proposal improves stale rate observability by enabling nodes to share stale tip data.  - Technical specifications include compressed headers, fork points, and limits on message size and cache.  - Tools like `staletip` help diagnose network issues, encourage feedback, and aid efficient branch reorganizations.

active_posts.title: [bitcoindev]
active_posts.summary: - A draft proposes standardizing enforcement policy formats for co-signers to improve blockchain interoperability.  - The draft includes diverse verification methods, script conditions, and accommodation for existing oracle attestations.  - Feedback is requested on technical concerns, policy structuring, and suitability of the proposed standardization layer.

active_posts.title: Unspendable keys in descriptors
active_posts.summary: - The integration of miniscript with taproot enables new wallet development possibilities but introduces unspendable key challenges.  - Multiple unspendable key generation methods exist, each with trade-offs in security, usability, and entropy requirements.  - Further discussion is needed to refine and develop cleaner standard solutions for creating unspendable keys.

active_posts.title: Gossip Observer: New project to monitor the Lightning P2P network
active_posts.summary: - The project observed reduced message convergence delay and identified connectivity and filtering inefficiencies within the network.  - Channel_update and node_announcement message analysis revealed significant propagation and volume concentration among few nodes.  - Future plans include expanding data collection infrastructure and encouraging community input for further metric analysis.

active_posts.title: Towards A K-of-N Lightning Network Node
active_posts.summary: - Nested MuSig2 enables k-of-n multisig in Lightning Network, increasing security and flexibility.  - Implementing k-of-n multisig requires BOLT protocol modifications and may pose privacy and efficiency risks.  - Proposed BOLT updates include new feature bits, improving compatibility and facilitating secure multisig operations.

today_in_history_posts.title: Mock introducing vulnerability in important Bitcoin projects
today_in_history_posts.summary: - Regular testing and verification of the review process are recommended to identify improvements and ensure effectiveness.  - An exercise will introduce vulnerabilities into three Bitcoin projects to evaluate the review system's performance.  - Results from these tests aim to increase security, though reputation differences may affect review attention.

today_in_history_posts.title: INTEROPERABILITY
today_in_history_posts.summary: - The proposal recommends establishing a decentralized integration lab for various Lightning Network implementations.  - Each team would provide a BOX with managed channels to all other implementations for testing.  - This initiative aims for thorough verification before public release and is considered business-critical.

today_in_history_posts.title: Thoughts on scaling and consensus changes (2023)
today_in_history_posts.summary: - Bitcoin scalability may require a distributed network of semi-trusted, interconnected off-chain entities for payments.  - Solutions prioritize auditing, fraud detection, affordable transactions, custody security, and integration with Layer 1.  - Supporting technologies, regulatory compliance, and resilient infrastructure are essential for effective and secure large-scale adoption.
